sections.overview: Parascyllium collare, the Collar Carpetshark, is an eastern Australian shark in family Parascylliidae.
sections.identification: It is brown with broad bands and a prominent dark collar behind the head.
sections.habitat: It lives on the eastern continental shelf, mainly around offshore rocky areas.
sections.diet: The species is poorly known, and the references consulted do not establish a detailed species-specific diet.
sections.behavior: It is a bottom-associated shark and is caught mainly as bycatch in some Australian trawl fisheries.
sections.reproduction: It is oviparous: females lay paired eggs, and embryos are nourished by yolk.
sections.ecology: Its close Australian relative, the Rusty Carpetshark, Parascyllium ferrugineum, ranges farther south and west and has rusty-brown markings rather than the Collar Carpetshark’s bold banding.
sections.conservation: Fishes of Australia reports an IUCN category of Least Concern. Bycatch occurs, and the species’ biology remains incompletely documented.
